hint.text: This image shows the god Ganesh. He has an elephant head and is one of the most well-known Hindu gods. Ganesh is the god of wisdom and learning and the remover of obstacles.

atoms.text: Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, is India’s biggest holiday. It is celebrated over 5 days. Different parts of India have different stories about how the holiday started, but they all light candles to protect themselves from spiritual darkness and to banish demons.
atoms.sound: Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights is India’s biggest holiday. It is celebrated over 5 days. Different parts of India have different stories about how the holiday started, but they all light candles to protect themselves from spiritual darkness and to banish demons.

atoms.text: Celebrating Diwali includes cleaning the home, buying golden forks and spoons for good luck, filling homes with clay lamps, wearing your finest clothes, setting off fireworks and eating delicious food with friends and family.
atoms.sound: Celebrating Diwali includes cleaning the home, buying golden forks and spoons for good luck, filling homes with clay lamps, wearing your finest clothes, setting off fireworks and eating delicious food with friends and family.

atoms.text: Diwali does not happen on the same days every year, but usually takes place in October or November. Diwali is a very popular and exciting holiday that many people look forward to all year long.
